retracted.name: Airtable
retracted.after_value: Azure, Box, ChatGPT, Claude, Dropbox, Ebay, GitHub, Google, Jira, Openai, Salesforce, Slack, Snowflake, Tableau, Virgin Voyages
retracted.summary: Customer logos first observed: "Azure, Box, ChatGPT, Claude, Dropbox, Ebay, GitHub, Google, Jira, Openai, Salesforce, S…"
retracted.retraction_reason: Airtable did not add a logo wall. The 11:10:09Z observation extracted no customer logos and the 15:53:34Z one extracted fifteen, and the index published that transition as an addition. A logo wall our extractor could not read and a logo wall that did not exist produce the same null, so the transition out of it cannot distinguish 'they added it' from 'we finally read it'. Rule S10 now records this as a signal acquisition and publishes nothing.

retracted.name: Notion
retracted.summary: Entry price moved from EUR 9.5 to USD 10
retracted.retraction_reason: Notion did not change its price. The 11:11:09Z observation was crawled from Germany and quoted EUR; the 11:18:26Z observation was crawled from a GitHub Actions runner in the US and quoted USD. notion.com/pricing selects currency by client IP. The crawl origin was not recorded at the time, and neither <html lang> nor the canonical URL moved, so the locale gate did not fire.

retracted.before_value: Free free | Plus EUR 9.5 | Business EUR 19.5 | Enterprise custom | Custom Agents USD 10/month
retracted.after_value: Free free | Plus USD 10 | Business USD 20 | Enterprise custom | Custom Agents USD 10/month
retracted.retraction_reason: Same cause as the entry-price retraction: the tier list was quoted in EUR from Germany and in USD from a US runner seven minutes later. The plans, their order and their prices were unchanged; only the currency the origin served differed.
